extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current students of The Second City Training Center (New York) — people interested in improv, sketch, stand-up, acting and comedy classes
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and policy guidance for prospective and current students about class selection, eligibility, auditions, payments, attendance, perks, and other administrative rules for Second City Training Center (New York).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservatory Program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have completed a full year of improv training (equivalent to our Improv Program) from another training centre and you have completed a post secondary acting course, then you are eligible to submit for our Conservatory Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission to the Conservatory is by audition only and requires previous experience; the Conservatory is described as the cornerstone program for aspiring professionals and qualifies you to audition for house teams and advanced programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditions / prerequisites for advanced programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only some advanced programs like the Sketch Conservatory require auditions, though some specialized classes and workshops may have prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditions apply primarily to advanced/specialized tracks; check specific class listings for prerequisites before registering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer classes in our Kids and Teens Program for students ages 4-18. Students must be at least 19 to attend classes in our adult programs or at least a high school graduate, but there is no upper age limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different age-based program streams exist (Kids & Teens vs adult programs); verify age eligibility before enrolling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition payment timing and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: We require payment at the time of registration in order to hold your spot in the class. Tuition is non-refundable and non-transferable. We accept Mastercard, Visa, Amex, cash, or cheque. PAYMENT PLANS AVAILABLE!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may register online and set up a payment plan or inquire with the office; payment secures your seat. Be aware that tuition is non-refundable/non-transferable (see transfer/refund policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers and refunds policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition fees are non-refundable and non-transferrable. If you have a conflict with your schedule, please contact our Customer Service team as soon as possible to see if any arrangements can be made. Transfers may be subject to a $25 transfer fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Customer Service promptly for schedule conflicts; although tuition is generally final, staff may assist and transfers (when allowed) often incur a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence and makeup class policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have to miss a class, please reach out to our Customer Service team for options. We do not offer scheduled makeup classes but will assist you as best we can. Make sure to contact your instructor for any material you may have missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are encouraged to attend all classes to avoid missing content and to contact instructors and Customer Service for materials or possible accommodations rather than expecting formal makeups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning student / re-entry placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Should this occur, please contact The Training Centre staff immediately. Please be informed that when you return, the Training Centre will place you at its discretion. Students who leave during the Conservatory Program may be asked to re-audition. Returning students must pay the tuition rate that is applicable to the time of rejoining The Training Centre. Any student returning after more than one (1) year of absence is required to rejoin the program at a level determined by The Training Centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-entry is handled case-by-case; expect possible re-auditioning and placement at staff discretion, and to pay current tuition rates when returning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class section naming / identification convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Why is there a random noun next to the class name? We have lots of classes, and sometimes we have multiple sections of the same class running at the same time. In those cases we add various words to the class names so you know which class you belong to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When continuing to the next level on the same day/time, enroll in the same word group to remain with the same cohort/instructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student perks and partner discounts eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Student perks (e.g., 'Bentwood 50% off your check', 'Second City Merchandise 15% off', 'Leon’s Bagels 15% off', 'Good Move 20% Drop-in classes') are available to students but often require proof of enrollment (class receipt and photo ID) and may be limited to one student (not per table) or otherwise restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring class receipt and picture ID to redeem discounts; check each partner's specific terms (per-student limits, codes, or required confirmation emails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rush ticket / student ticket policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Student Rush Tickets: Current students can redeem one free ticket if they arrive, in person, at the box office within two hours before the start of the show. These tickets are only redeemable for Grad Revue shows and cannot be reserved for guests. Also: a limited number of $10 tickets will go on sale at 10am on the day of the performance. Tickets are available on a first-come, first-served basis and can only be purchased in person at The Second City box office. Tickets are limited to ONE ticket per student. Students must present valid proof of enrollment. We cannot hold spots or process reservations over the phone. All rush ticket sales are final and cannot be refunded, exchanged or replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rush tickets require in-person purchase, proof of enrollment, strict one-ticket-per-student limits, and are final sale—plan accordingly and arrive early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for choosing a starting program
rubrics_metrics.description: WHERE DO I BEGIN? It depends what you’d like to do. The Improvisation Program is a great jumping off point. We also have Improv for Anxiety, Public Speaking and Acting as great first options. Or if you’re looking to go the writing route, we have the Writing or Stand Up Programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select classes based on goals: improv for broad foundation, acting to apply improv to scripted work, writing/stand-up for a writing-focused path; staff can advise by phone if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Acting and Improv classes
rubrics_metrics.description: While both of these core programs use similar improvisational techniques derived from the teachings of Viola Spolin, the focus for the performer is different. In the Improv program, we teach you how to work, play & perform without a script. In the Acting program, we show you how to use those improv skills to be a better, more present actor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Acting if your goal is scripted performance and character work; choose Improv if you want unscripted performance skills and spontaneity. Later acting levels incorporate scripts and Second City Archive scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway and expectations for becoming a Second City cast member
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes a great deal of training and experience to become a member of our professional company. Most of the resident actors have trained and performed for a number of years before being hired by The Second City. Although many of the resident company actors are graduates of The Training Centre, completion of any program does not guarantee employment with the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Conservatory is the most direct preparation and can qualify you to audition for house teams; long-term training, experience, and auditioning are required—there is no guarantee of hiring upon graduation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome communication and teacher/room assignment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A Welcome email with your room and teacher assignment will be sent to you withing 24 hours of your first class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect administrative details by email shortly after your first attendance; contact Customer Service if you do not receive assignment information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events, jams and open mics access
rubrics_metrics.description: Jams + Open Mics: The one-stop-shop for all student jams, open mics, workshops, and special events! Come to play or to watch. Events are recommended for current students only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These events are primarily intended for students; check the schedule and be aware that some events may be restricted to current enrollees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship availability
rubrics_metrics.description: ARE THERE SCHOLARSHIPS? Yes! You can find more information here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarships exist—contact the Training Centre or follow the provided scholarship information link for details and application procedures.
